# MirrorMate 2.1.0

MirrorMate now runs on macOS and Windows alongside Ubuntu and Debian. This release adds Homebrew mirrors and dedicated platform managers for installation and maintenance.

## Highlights

- **macOS:** configure Python/PyPI, NPM, Go, and Homebrew mirrors from the CLI or TUI.
- **Windows:** configure Python/PyPI, NPM, and Go mirrors with native user configuration paths. The TUI dependency, `windows-curses`, is installed automatically.
- **Homebrew:** change bottle and optional API endpoints through `brew.env`, preserve unrelated settings, preview changes, create backups, restore previous files, or select official endpoints again.
- **Platform managers:** `manager-mac.sh`, `manager-linux.sh`, and `manager.ps1` support `install`, `update`, `uninstall`, and `status`. They require root/Administrator privileges and exit with instructions when elevation is missing.
- **Platform-aware dashboard:** unavailable services are hidden from the default dashboard, list, and status output; explicit unsupported configuration commands explain the limitation.
- **Portable backups:** restore checks use the same configuration paths as adapters, with additional validation for Windows paths.

## Install

On macOS or Ubuntu/Debian:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/free-programmers/MirrorMate/main/install.sh | sudo bash
```

On Windows, open **PowerShell as Administrator**:

```powershell
& ([scriptblock]::Create((Invoke-RestMethod https://raw.githubusercontent.com/free-programmers/MirrorMate/main/manager.ps1)))
```

Linux installation uses the latest `.deb` release and checks its SHA-256 checksum. Mac and Windows managers install the current `main` source archive in an isolated machine-wide Python environment and require Python 3.10+ with venv and pip to be installed first. Run the installed `mirrormate` command as your normal user for user-level mirror changes.

The Python wheel and source distribution are also attached for manual installation. `python-packages.sha256` verifies those files. Manager scripts are attached as standalone assets.

## Examples

```bash
mirrormate status --json
mirrormate set python --mirror pypi-official --backup
mirrormate set homebrew --url https://mirror.example.com/homebrew-bottles --api-url https://mirror.example.com/api --dry-run
mirrormate set homebrew --mirror homebrew-official --backup
```

Replace example mirror URLs with the endpoints supplied by your mirror provider. Homebrew commands apply to macOS.

## Compatibility and upgrade notes

- Python 3.10+ remains required. CI targets Python 3.10 on Linux/macOS and Python 3.12 on Windows.
- APT and Docker daemon configuration remain Linux-only. Use Docker Desktop's **Settings > Docker Engine** on macOS and Windows.
- Homebrew Git remotes, taps, and artifact proxy settings are outside the mirror adapter's scope.
- Manager uninstall actions preserve user settings, mirror choices, and backups. Existing pipx or other manual installations can be maintained separately; managers refuse to overwrite conflicting managed locations or commands.
- README and Python package metadata now match the existing GPL v3 license file. The license file itself has not changed.

See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/free-programmers/MirrorMate/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for the complete change list.
